source_snapshot.test_name_items: SEL logs- check for hot plug in /out storage decive
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Plug in /out the storage device and observe the sel log each action

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
all message & info should match status during plug in / out the storage device.
if no relative sel log appear need submit the bug since high user impact.

historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 861/2291 accepts the truncated read-only command as agent-direct, while its own text acknowledges the physical operator action; it does not analyze the data/RAID hazard, target identity, incomplete filtering, stale-event attribution, action order or recovery.

original_test_intent: Verify that removal and insertion of the exact Project-approved hot-pluggable storage device each produce the correct BMC SEL record or record sequence for that bay/device and action, with message, sensor identity, event direction/status and timing consistent with the actual physical transition.
original_method: The preserved source calls for clearing logs, then physically plugging the storage device out and in while observing SEL after each action. The Review layer keeps both functional actions but replaces blanket evidence deletion with complete baseline capture plus a stable last-record/sequence boundary before each action; it requires a qualified operator, verified quiesced non-boot target, separately timed removal and insertion, full post-action records and controlled restoration.
manual_activity: A qualified operator identifies and verifies the exact serviceable storage device and bay, quiesces it under the approved controller/OS procedure, physically removes it and later reinserts it at the two authorized checkpoints, and stops on unexpected resistance, latch, power or service behavior. Automation can capture and correlate BMC/host/controller evidence but cannot substitute a log read for either physical action.
required_inputs: Exact device serial/model/protocol, bay/slot/port, backplane, controller/RAID/HBA and BMC sensor mapping
Project proof that the populated device/bay supports hot removal and insertion in the specified host power and controller mode
Approved action order, workload/I/O quiescence, filesystem/mount/swap/LVM/device-mapper/RAID membership and redundancy/rebuild checks
Data disposition, backup or disposable media, maintenance window, operator access, service-impact acceptance and OOB/storage recovery plan
Expected removal and insertion SEL record IDs/sensor/type/event data, assert/deassert semantics, order, allowed latency and any platform-defined absence behavior
Validated SEL interface/client, supported authentication/cipher, protected secrets, BMC/host time synchronization and complete record-boundary collection method
safety_requirements: Never remove an unknown, boot, EFI, mounted, swap, LVM, device-mapper, active-I/O or unapproved RAID member. Stop if identity, redundancy, rebuild state or hot-plug capability is uncertain.
Do not clear SEL, kernel or controller logs to create a baseline. Preserve complete existing evidence and mark the last stable record ID/count/sequence immediately before each physical action.

Do not use a text grep or `tail -20` as completeness proof. Vendor records may not contain the guessed English words, related entries may span more than twenty records and stale matching events can be misattributed.
Treat removal and insertion as distinct approved actions with separate timestamps, record boundaries, health checks and stop decisions; one action's event cannot prove the other.
Do not expose BMC passwords with `-P`, assume cipher suite 17 or weaken TLS. Use a validated protected credential/session path and retain stdout, stderr and exit status separately.

Perform no automatic retry or repeated hot-plug cycle. Stop on wrong target, failed quiescence, unexpected array degradation, missing/ambiguous event, device not returning, new critical logs or controller/host instability; invoke the approved recovery and preserve evidence.
agent_execution_scope: Before any action, bind the physical device to OS/controller/BMC identities, verify hot-plug support and data safety, snapshot full SEL information/records and host/controller health, and present the exact removal plan for approval.

After the qualified operator performs one approved removal, capture the full new SEL interval and host/controller state; correlate canonical record IDs, raw event data, sensor, direction/status and timestamp with the recorded removal time.

Only if the removal checkpoint and system state are safe, request/confirm the separately defined insertion step, then collect a new complete interval and prove the device returns to the approved controller/OS/RAID state.
Report missing, extra, late or ambiguously decoded events and any recovery action as facts for engineer triage; do not submit a bug autonomously and never issue DUT PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the exact removable target, topology, Project hot-plug method, action sequence, service state, data-safety checks, maintenance window and recovery/abort thresholds.
Provide the authoritative removal/insertion SEL event matrix, decoder/SDR context, allowed timing and whether assert/deassert or multiple ordered records are expected.
Review separate physical, SEL and host/controller evidence for both actions, decide whether absent/mismatched events require a defect, and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unfit as the test method: it performs no hot-plug action, cannot bind records to the exact device or action boundary, can miss OEM/non-text events and truncates extended output. It also exposes a password, assumes cipher 17 and incorrectly labels a data-bearing physical operation no-risk.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the Project-approved hot-plug procedure for the verified device/bay. Before each separately approved operator action, capture a full SEL boundary and synchronized host/controller state; afterward retrieve all records beyond that boundary through the validated protected interface and correlate canonical event data with the action timestamp and device identity.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The storage plug-out/plug-in actions, per-action SEL observation, message/status Criteria, high-impact missing-event escalation, generic pre-clear text, absent Script and 10/0-minute estimates remain preserved; the Review layer rejects evidence deletion and partial grep/tail output without reducing either physical checkpoint.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Run two gated checkpoints—approved removal and approved insertion—on one verified hot-pluggable non-system device, using stable pre-action SEL sequence boundaries and complete post-action BMC plus host/controller correlation without clearing logs.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the designated bay/device/controller combination documented as hot-pluggable in the selected host power, RAID/HBA and service state.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware/SDR, controller firmware/driver, backplane, storage firmware, OS/kernel and SEL client/decoder versions because event identity and hot-plug behavior are platform-specific.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Project storage serviceability procedure, controller/backplane/device hot-plug specification, platform SEL sensor/event map and recovery runbook.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Retains physical removal and insertion but protects data and prior evidence, creates deterministic record boundaries and validates canonical OEM events rather than keyword fragments.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Read-only SEL inspection is only supporting evidence; removal coverage does not prove insertion, host enumeration does not prove BMC logging and a matching text line does not prove the expected device, direction or complete event sequence.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Target/topology and data safety, service state/action order, authoritative event matrix, validated collection path, operator approval and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A wrong or active device can corrupt data or degrade an array; redundant events, delayed BMC timestamps and vendor decoding can confuse correlation; physical damage or a non-returning device may require OOB/manual recovery.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use Redfish, a vendor log decoder or another approved tool instead of ipmitool, but must record the preserved CLI proposal, actual interface/version, substitution reason, engineer approval, complete event equivalence and any unverified tool-specific coverage. It may define an insertion-first sequence only when physically meaningful and documented; it may not omit removal or insertion and claim full original coverage.
expected_evidence: BMC/chassis/host and device serial/model/protocol plus bay/port/backplane/controller/RAID-HBA-to-SEL-sensor identity map
Hot-plug capability proof, pre-action mount/swap/LVM/device-mapper/RAID/I-O/rebuild/redundancy state, data disposition and explicit operator approvals
Complete baseline SEL metadata/records and separate stable record-ID/count/sequence boundaries with synchronized removal and insertion timestamps
For each action, full new raw/decoded records showing sensor, event type/data, assert/deassert or status, order and allowed latency against the approved matrix
Post-removal and post-insertion OS/controller/RAID/device state, unexpected kernel/controller/BMC logs, service impact and final restored topology/health
Protected command audit with client/interface versions, stdout/stderr/exit status, no-clear/no-retry proof, recovery/defect-triage notes and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require storage removal/insertion with matching SEL events. The blanket pre-test clear is an unsafe method defect, and the target/event details are incomplete Project inputs, but neither changes the identifiable purpose or creates an irreconcilable source contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The target operation and required evidence are understandable. Missing device/topology, serviceability, event mapping, credentials and recovery are resolvable Project execution-readiness inputs, so the review is PACKAGE rather than permanently BLOCKED; execution remains prohibited until resolved.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes YES to PACKAGE, rejects the filtered recent read and no-risk claim, and restores both physical actions, exact target safety, complete event correlation and recovery.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with its hybrid classification and storage-safety model while sharpening per-action boundaries, separate removal/insertion acceptance, engineer-owned defect filing and no-repeat behavior.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces agent-direct treatment of a read-only lookup with a qualified-operator physical workflow plus bounded full-record and host/controller evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No prior invalid draft exists for this sequence.

review_improvement: Prevents a stale keyword match or twenty-record tail from being mistaken for storage hot-plug coverage, prevents removal of an unsafe device and preserves independent proof for both removal and insertion without erasing historical evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A storage hot-plug event is a cross-domain transition: the physical bay, controller/OS device and BMC sensor must resolve to the same component. Removal and insertion can produce different assert/deassert or OEM record sequences, so each needs its own before/after boundary and topology evidence. Clearing the SEL is unnecessary and destructive; stable record IDs and timestamps isolate new events while preserving history. Because the stimulus is physical and can damage data availability, automation can observe and correlate but cannot execute or repeat it autonomously.
